description: Compare nightly hotel rate to hotel_rate_caps.csv for the destination city. Exceptions can be legitimate, but should be reviewed if materially over cap.
Flights should generally be booked at least 7 days before domestic travel and 14 days before international travel. Treat as an opportunity signal, not a hard violation.
Airfare and hotel spend should usually link back to a TMC booking, OBT search, or clear reason for direct booking.
Large card transactions should have a matching expense line or clear offsetting credit/refund. Duplicate expenses for the same receipt should be reviewed.
Travel by inactive employees or missing HR identities should be reviewed before payment or reimbursement.
Card/expense activity during a trip should generally align with the origin, destination, or normal transit path. Unexpected cities are review-worthy, not automatically wrong.
Hotel check-in/check-out should roughly align with flight dates. Extra nights may be valid but should be explainable.
Canceled segments, refunds, ticket credits, and reissued fares should be netted carefully to avoid double-counting.
